Privacy Policy

FE fundinfo (UK) Limited (“we”, “our”, “us” and derivatives, “FE fundinfo”) is committed to protecting and respecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy, together with our Terms of Use, sets out the basis on which any personal data that we collect from you, or that you provide to us, will be processed by us relating to your use of this FE fundinfo site (“site”), which contains information about many different investment funds and trusts, managed and registered in many different locations around the world, governed by various laws and regulations.

For the purposes of the Data Protection Act 1998, the data controller is FE fundinfo (UK) Limited of 7 Chertsey Road, Woking, Surrey, GU21 5AB. Our nominated representative for the purpose of this Act is Kirsty Witter.

Information We May Collect From You

We may collect and process the following data about you when you register with us or visit our site:

  • Information that you provide to us when you register and set up a user name, password and e-mail address.
  • Details of your visits to our site including, but not limited to, traffic data, location data, and other communication data, and the resources that you access.
  • Information about your computer, including where available your IP address, operating system and browser type, for system administration and to improve the structure and content of our site. In order to provide support for FE Analytics, our support team need access to all information provided in relation to this tool.

How we use information

We store and use information you provide as follows:

  • To present content effectively.
  • To carry out our obligations arising from any contracts between you and us.
  • To enable you to participate in interactive features of our service, when you choose to do so
  • To notify you about changes to our service.
  • To improve our content by tracking group information that describes the habits, usage, patterns and demographics of our customers.

We will not disclose your name, email address or postal address or any data that could identify you to any third party without first receiving your permission. However, you agree that we may disclose to any regulatory authority to which we are subject and to any investment exchange on which we may deal or to its related clearing house (or to investigators, inspectors or agents appointed by them), or to any person empowered to require such information by or under any legal enactment, any information they may request or require relating to you, or if relevant, any of your clients.

Cookies

A cookie is a text-only string of information that a website transfers to the cookie file of the browser on your computer's hard disk so that the website can remember who you are.

A cookie will typically contain the name of the domain from which the cookie has come, the "lifetime" of the cookie, and a value, usually a randomly generated unique number. Most major websites use cookies. Cookies cannot be used by themselves to identify you.

In order to provide personalised services and analyse site traffic, we may use a cookie file which is stored on your browser or the hard drive of your computer. Some of the cookies we use are essential for the site to operate.

Most web browsers allow some control of most cookies through the browser settings. To find out more about cookies, including how to see what cookies have been set and how to manage and delete them, visit www.allaboutcookies.org.

You can block cookies by activating the setting on your browser (within the “Help” section of your browser) which allows you to refuse the setting of all or some cookies. However, if you use your browser settings to block all cookies (including essential cookies) you may not be able to access all or part of our site. Unless you have adjusted your browser setting so that it will refuse cookies, our system will issue cookies as soon as you visit our site.

Two types of cookies are used by us on our site:

  • Session Cookies: which are temporary cookies that remain in the cookie file of your browser until you leave the site
  • Persistent cookies: which remain in the cookie file of your browser for much longer (though how long will depend on the lifetime of the specific cookie).

Session Cookies allow you to carry information across pages of our site and avoid having to re-enter information and to allow you to access stored information.

Persistent Cookies help us recognise you as a unique visitor when you return to our website and to allow us to tailor content to avoid you changing information repeatedly. All FE fundinfo persistent cookies have a 1 month lifecycle.

Use Of Cookies By FE fundinfo

  • Login details. These cookies are used by the login page to remember the last used login details when the user clicks ‘Remember me’.
  • Remembering any interaction with the basket, shortlist and portfolio sections of the site.

Where We Store Your Personal Data

The data that we collect from you may be transferred to, and stored at, a destination outside the European Economic Area (“EEA”). It may be processed by staff operating outside the EEA who work for us or for one of our suppliers. Such staff may be engaged in, amongst other things, the provision of support services. By agreeing to the use of cookies and by submitting your personal data, you agree to this transfer, storing and processing. We will take all steps reasonably necessary, including the use of encryption, to ensure that your data is treated securely and in accordance with this privacy policy.

All information you provide to us is stored on our secure servers. Where we have given you (or where you have chosen) a password which enables you to access certain parts of our site, you are responsible for keeping this password confidential. We ask you not to share a password with anyone.

Unfortunately, the transmission of information via the internet is not completely secure. Although we will do our best to protect your personal data, we cannot guarantee the security of your data transmitted to our site; any transmission is at your own risk. Once we have received your information, we will use strict procedures and security features to try to prevent unauthorized access.

Changes To Our Privacy Policy

Any changes we make to our privacy policy in the future will be posted on this page.

Other Websites

Our site might contains links to other websites. If you follow a link to any of these websites, please note that these websites have their own privacy policies and that we do not accept any responsibility or liability for these policies. Please check these policies before you submit any personal data to these websites.

Contact

If you want more information or have any questions or comments relating to our privacy policy, please email CustomerSupport@fefundinfo.com in the first instance.

Ongoing charge 
Ongoing charge – is levied by fund management companies and varies depending on the funds chosen. These ongoing charges are in addition to any product or adviser charges. If the ongoing charge figure (OCF) is not available, we show the total expense ratio (TER). Both include a fixed management fee plus expenses that vary with the day to day running of the fund. The OCF includes some one-off charges that aren’t in the TER, but the two measures are very similar.

Sector - there is a huge variety of funds on sale in the UK. The Investment Association sectors provide a way of dividing around 3,000 of these funds into broad groups. Investors and their advisers can then compare funds in one or more sectors before looking in detail at individual funds.
 Ongoing charge 
Ongoing charge – is levied by fund management companies and varies depending on the funds chosen. These ongoing charges are in addition to any product or adviser charges. If the ongoing charge figure (OCF) is not available, we show the total expense ratio (TER). Both include a fixed management fee plus expenses that vary with the day to day running of the fund. The OCF includes some one-off charges that aren’t in the TER, but the two measures are very similar.
 KID/KIID 
Key Information Documents (KIDs) and Key Investor Information Documents (KIIDs) - These documents give a short overview of the fund. They explain its objectives and how it invests, aiming to make it easier for you to understand each fund's key features and to compare different funds.
 Factsheet 
Factsheet – A short fund overview which includes important information such as the fund objective, charges, recent fund performance, mix of investments and key investment risks.
 Prospectus 
Prospectus – A detailed overview of the fund and it’s investment process.
 Prospectus Supplement Consumer Facing Disclosure Report 
Consumer Facing Disclosure Report - Gives details about a fund's approach to sustainability. It’s available where a fund has been designated as meeting a defined set of sustainability criteria. As this designation is voluntary, some funds will incorporate responsible investment considerations into their investment process, but won't make a Consumer Facing Disclosure Report available.
Sustainability Label 
Sustainability label – Funds that meet certain sustainability criteria may apply for one of four sustainability labels. These are: Sustainability Focus, Sustainability Impact, Sustainability Improvers and Sustainability Mixed Goals. Find out more about the sustainability labels . Please note that these labels are available to funds on a voluntary basis, and aren’t open to all fund types. Some funds consider responsible investment factors in their investment process, but don’t have a sustainability label.
 Missing UK SDR Label Reason 
Missing UK Sustainability Disclosure Requirements (SDR) label reason - The SDR regime comprises a robust anti-greenwashing rule, four non-hierarchical investment labels, and comprehensive disclosure and marketing guidelines. It aims to empower investors with greater clarity and confidence in making informed decisions about their sustainable investments.

Fund name FE fundinfo crown rating 
FE fundinfo crown rating - enables investors to distinguish between funds that are strongly outperforming their benchmark and those that are not.
The top 10% of funds will be awarded five FE fundinfo Crowns, the next 15% receiving four Crowns and each of the remaining three quartiles will be given three, two and one Crown(s) respectively.
 FundCalibre 
FundCalibre - FundCalibre is a ratings business that uses a forward looking quant model to identify funds for consideration for a rating. The research team then conducts meetings with fund managers to see if the fund deserves to be rated. FundCalibre's Elite Rating is typically awarded to no more than 10% of funds in any sector.

Name Sustainability Label 
Sustainability label - Funds that meet certain sustainability criteria may apply for one of four sustainability labels. These are: Sustainability Focus, Sustainability Impact, Sustainability Improvers and Sustainability Mixed Goals. Please note that these labels are available to funds on a voluntary basis, and aren’t open to all fund types. Some funds consider responsible investment factors in their investment process, but don’t have a sustainability label.
 Missing UK SDR Label Reason 
Missing UK SDR Label Reason - Not all funds will qualify for a label. This column will explain the reason why.
 Overseas Sustainable Fund 
If Overseas Sustainable Fund is set to ‘Yes’ this product is based overseas and is not subject to UK sustainable investment labelling and disclosure requirements. Further information on sustainable investment labels and what these mean can be found on the FCA Website
 Sustainability Impact 
Sustainability Impact – These funds must aim to achieve a predefined, positive, measurable environmental and/or social impact. The percentage figures shown represent the proportion of the fund that qualifies for this label. Funds in the Sustainability Impact category may qualify under one label only.
 Sustainability Focus 
Sustainability Focus - These funds must invest in assets that are environmentally or socially sustainable, determined by a robust, evidence-based standard of sustainability. The percentage figures shown represent the proportion of the fund that qualifies for this label. Funds in the Sustainability Focus category may qualify under one label only. The fund must invest at least 70% of its assets in accordance with this sustainability objective.
 Sustainability Improvers 
Sustainability Improvers - These funds must invest in assets that have the potential become more sustainable over time, determined by their potential to meet a robust, evidence based standard of sustainability over time. The percentage figures shown represent the proportion of the fund that qualifies for this label. Funds in the Sustainability Improvers category may qualify under one label only. The fund must invest at least 70% of its assets in accordance with this sustainability objective.
 Sustainability Mixed Goals 
Mixed Goals - These funds must invest in assets that meet, or have the potential to meet, a robust, evidence-based standard for sustainability, and/ or invest with an aim to achieve positive impact. The percentage figures shown represent the proportion of the fund that qualifies for this label. Funds in the Mixed Goals category may have a proportion of the fund that meets the criteria in the other sustainability categories.
 Consumer Facing Disclosure Report 
Consumer Facing Disclosure Report - Gives details about a fund's approach to sustainability. It’s available where a fund has been designated as meeting a defined set of sustainability criteria. As this designation is voluntary, some funds will incorporate responsible investment considerations into their investment process, but won't make a Consumer Facing Disclosure Report available.
 Pre-Contractual Disclosure Report Periodic Disclosure Report Reporting Date Uses ESG IN Marketing UK SDR 
Uses ESG IN Marketing UK SDR - Not all funds that are responsibly investing will qualify or choose to use a label however this flags that this is a responsibly invested fund.

(*) Performance figures for funds with less than 1 years history will not be displayed.

Past performance
All fund data is provided by FE fundinfo (UK) Limited. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. The value of an investment and the income from it can fall as well as rise for a number of reasons, for example market and currency movements. You could get back less than originally invested. If you’re unsure whether a fund is right for you, or you need further help, please seek advice or guidance.

Performance data explained
Performance figures are calculated on a bid price to bid price basis (mid to mid for OEICs), include fund charges and are updated to the most recent price date available unless stated otherwise. All of the performance data is measured in percentage terms and is shown over various time periods to show how funds have performed. ‘Cumulative performance’ provides a cumulative sum of fund performance over three months, six months and one, three and five year periods, where the fund has been in existence for over 12 months. ’Discrete performance’ provides a breakdown of fund performance for each respective twelve month period to the end of the last calendar quarter, over the last five years, or as many years as we have if less than five years.

Important information
If you wish to invest, or top up an existing investment, in any of the funds shown please ensure you read the relevant fund Key Investor Information Document (KIID), or PRIIPs Key Information Document (KID) if available, and any other relevant fund information documents. Please remember that charges exist on investments that will affect performance figures. For more information on the fund charges you pay please see the relevant KIID/KID for your fund.
